preceding_agent.question: Does the current focused-task selector improve learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic task choice?
preceding_agent.research_result: Process-audit conclusion (LEARNING_PROCESS): the primary question resolves to NO DEMONSTRATED SELECTOR ADVANTAGE. The frontier-first selection principle shows a real descriptive information-flow benefit over the single documented opportunistic activation (coherent, non-redundant, independently verified cell closures plus the first positive candidate), but a causal advantage is not established (n=1 baseline; framework-maturity, cell-choice and circularity confounds). More decisively, this activation verified a concrete implementation defect: the controller re-selected P-001 (completed and controller-validated with RETAIN at slot 1) for slot 3 instead of advancing to P-002, because P-001 was left OPEN at selection time (proved by the identical compared_against candidate lists and by an isolated controller probe). The selection principle is retained (RETAIN) - it is not refuted and the defect is a fixable state-transition bug - but the process should be IMPROVED: the controller task-lifecycle transition must move a task completed with RETAIN/REJECT/VERIFIED_NEGATIVE_RESULT out of OPEN so it cannot be re-selected. That fix requires control-plane authority over .github/scripts and is therefore handed off rather than implemented here. No numerical reward score or controller redesign is proposed (out of scope).
preceding_agent.uncertainty_reduced: Reduced uncertainty about the descriptive question (the frontier-first record is coherent, non-redundant and independently verified, with the opportunistic baseline confirmed n=1 and UNVERIFIED) and established a concrete, controller-side-verified selector defect (duplicate P-001 assignment at slot 3). Did not reduce uncertainty about the exact root cause of the stale OPEN status or about causal superiority.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_targeted: Whether explicit highest-value focused-task (frontier-first) selection causally improves learning efficiency relative to prior opportunistic, queue-driven task choice.
unverified: Causal superiority of frontier-first selection over opportunistic choice is NOT demonstrated: n=1 opportunistic baseline, framework-maturity confound (full gate stack existed before the frontier-first cells), cell-choice confound (the first positive candidate may reflect the momentum signal class rather than the procedure), and selection circularity (the frontier/queue is authored by the worker and the ranking is reconstructed post hoc).

Exact mechanism by which P-001 remained OPEN at slot-3 selection is not established: the controller's select_task only transitions the immediately preceding agent's task, so a RETAIN at slot 1 should have set P-001 RESOLVED. Whether the status transition was not applied, or the queue was reset between slots, requires a controller execution trace.
